productionRelease.note: DASH.13 is the increment that approved an intentional public production deployment. Approval makes production a SUPPORTED target; it does not make it the DEFAULT one. project.environment above is still staging, and no edit to this file alone can point the tooling at production: targeting it requires --environment production and --confirm-production on the command line, and the tooling refuses production without both. Staging keeps every safeguard it had — it remains non-production, robots-disallowed and preview-marked, and is never deleted or repurposed as a side effect of a production release.
productionRelease.buildArgumentNote: The canonical origin and the indexing policy are resolved from RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT_NAME and RAILWAY_PUBLIC_DOMAIN at BUILD time for every statically prerendered route, and at request time for a dynamic one. A production deployment must therefore be a FRESH BUILD carrying production build arguments. Promoting or re-running an image built in another environment ships a deployment whose robots.txt and page metadata disagree — DASH.13 reproduced exactly that. scripts/railway/verify_release_policy.ts detects it from outside.

ssl.note: Railway's postgres-ssl image terminates TLS itself and issues its own certificate; SSL_CERT_DAYS is one of the variables it publishes. The provisioning job additionally asserts the session is encrypted rather than trusting the image.

tcpProxy.purpose: External reachability for a future Microsoft Fabric connection. Not used by the website, which has no database connection at all.

databaseSetup.name: arpi-database-setup
databaseSetup.note: Runs the repository's ordered SQL sequence, creates the login roles, loads the deterministic development profile and verifies the result, then exits. It is not a backend API: it serves no traffic, has no public domain, no health check, and a NEVER restart policy so a completed run is not restarted into a loop.

serviceDependencies.reason: The provisioning job reads the database over the project's private network using reference variables. Nothing is copied.

deliberatelyAbsent.backendWebService: The ARPI architecture has no general-purpose backend. The website is seventeen routes with no runtime data source: the reference and utility pages are statically prerendered, and the nine operating routes are server-rendered on demand because their state is a URL query, not because they reach for data — every figure comes from committed generated datasets read at render time. A backend would be a service with nothing to serve. Corrected in DASH.13: this field previously said 'fourteen statically prerendered routes', which was true before the operating application gained URL-addressable filters.
deliberatelyAbsent.websiteDatabaseAccess: The website holds no database credential, opens no connection, and is not granted a reference to one. Verified by scripts/railway/verify_railway_configuration.ts.
deliberatelyAbsent.productionEnvironment: Approved by DASH.13 and still absent at the time this file was written. It is listed here because its absence remains a deliberate state rather than an oversight: approval makes production a supported target, and creating it is a separate act that requires --environment production and --confirm-production. Until it exists, staging is the only deployed environment and is correctly non-indexable.
deliberatelyAbsent.prEnvironments: Evaluated and deliberately not enabled; see deployment/railway/README.md section 9.
